what: the first wave of ports made from the guide alone, for perl and swift: each ported, read by an independent reviewer, fixed, and verified

Records read: s3b-port-perl, s3b-review-perl, s3b-fix-perl, s3b-verify-perl, s3b-port-swift, s3b-review-swift, s3b-fix-swift, s3b-verify-swift (all .txt, all present). Stage briefs read for purpose: prompts/j-port.md, j-review.md, j-fix.md, k-verify.md, plus brief.md.

rounds.purpose: Port perl's README tutorial, root quick start and REFERENCE to the shared pages by following the guide alone: naming hook, syntax provider, porter's part of the forms file, deletion of the three old components; check the runtime table against the runtime; record interface gaps without bending the interface.

findings.finding: Neither provider reads the model, and very little of each page is the language's own prose. perl: notes 1.6% and provider literals 1.8% of words. swift: 0 notes, provider literals 0.6%. But swift-only words reach 35.6% of the tutorial and 92% of the root quick start, all from shared wrapped-style sentences only swift prints, which the reviewer calls relocated per-language prose that nothing compares.

perl exposed a real interface limit. One imports printer serves both the tutorial and the root quick start and cannot tell them apart, so all 19 NEW root quick starts lost `use lib 'perl/lib'` and fail `perl -c` from the repository root. The fix is additive shared code (a place on Scope plus a directory role). No breaking change is needed.
findings.source: s3b-review-perl.txt: required_fixes[1], hypotheses H4; s3b-verify-perl.txt: still_wrong[0]

findings.finding: The example lanes did not catch the perl regressions. perl's runner prepends the import and replaces the constructor, so a missing import, wrong constructor options or wrong call arguments (verifier's `load('id' => 'planet_id')`) all pass 7/7. The lane also passed a shared showFields change that prints HASH(0x...) in 17 variations.

After the fixes the perl port fails its own one command on purpose: 14 defect classes wait for 3 shared changes. Every other check passes: ledger OPEN 0, blocks OPEN 0, purity 0, guard 4/4, suite 2596/0/5. The verifier confirmed both defects by running them.

swift could not be compiled anywhere. 172 changed blocks are verified by no compiler, there is no swift README lane, and the generated swift README test checks only that delimiters balance. H4 is untested for swift.

swift was the first language to print the wrapped result style, so its shared sentences had never been printed before. The reference-comparison nets are empty for it. Dropping a shared sentence from one or all variations moved no number in from-scratch mode. Several attacks were caught only by the porter's own hand records, which a new port does not have.

The guard has blind spots that the independent rounds found. Citations match on word tokens, so a quote that does not show its value passes. The record expression is checked only by its trailing name: swift's attempted whole-record fix was defeated by `({var}.asNative)?.data()`. There is no check of call arity: `load(nil)` against two required parameters passed.

portcheck can report PASS on a stale build. A provider that failed to compile left the old build in place and portcheck still passed. A generation that threw printed 'regenerated 0 variations' and every number was measured on stale pages, because the pipe drops gen.js's exit code. The fix is in the shared tools and was recorded, not made.

Some true runtime facts could not be printed through the existing shared sentences. swift's matchv copy is declared and guarded but ReadmeRef's matchArg sentence ignores it. swift's list sentence lost OLD's working `list(nil, nil)` and now names `list()`, which Swift cannot call. The second fix is a breaking sentence change that alters every ported provider's list wording.

Catalogued corrections arrived from shared code with no per-language edit in both ports. perl: S49, S50, S25, U34, U45, ref-6, md-cell, S09. swift: S49, S50, S09, S13, S25, U34, U43, U45, G27. This was read, not audited against the catalogue. The perl porter mis-cited S13 for the log default (it is S09). Two new uncatalogued regressions came from shared code.
findings.source: s3b-review-perl.txt: hypotheses H3; s3b-review-swift.txt: hypotheses H3

findings.finding: The independent rounds corrected the builders' reports every time. Both porters reported ok true. The reviewers found false or weak facts in both: perl's stream note was false under chunked streaming, and swift's body.values named the wrong constructor. The swift fixer's claim that the record check was complete was overstated. Both verifiers returned ok false.

Interface change counts for this wave. perl: 0 breaking, 2 additive and 1 shared behaviour fix. swift: 2 breaking, both changed sentences (the wrapped unwrap, which forces no other provider, and the list no-match call, which changes every provider's wording), plus additive guard and tools changes. The verifier's final list has 7 shared changes. No shared change was made in this wave.
